On the inner-being lens, the arena is the malicious persecutor: this reading indicts the wicked's interior (directive 5) - a man who, far from pitying, actively hunted the poor and crushed. Held with its passage-mates (poor #5, brokenhearted H3512), it forms the threefold portrait of the persecuted low whose very helplessness the enemy exploited.
narratives.story: The poet accuses his enemy of a specific cruelty: he hunted down the poor, the needy, and the brokenhearted - chasing the very people least able to defend themselves. Here neediness is the mark of a helpless victim, someone the wicked man exploited rather than pitied. The need stands together with poverty and a crushed heart, a threefold portrait of the defenceless. The horror is that this weakness, which should have drawn mercy, instead drew persecution. It exposes the dark heart of the oppressor.
narratives.variation_note: Sixth of eight readings of H0034:needy (ebyon). Here (Ps 109:16) the needy are the VICTIM PURSUED by a cruel enemy ('he pursued the poor and needy'), operation 'be pursued', target 'by the enemy'. It differs from #1 (heard), #2 (urgent plea), #3 (deliver from wicked), #4 (casting self on God), #5 (raised), #7 (pleading before God), #8 (lifted). Distinctive: neediness as the object of active persecution - the enemy hounds the poor, needy and brokenhearted to death.

narratives.narrative: This is the family's second Hebrew word for 'brokenhearted' (kaah, distinct from H7665's shabar-heart). The sense (101) is 'brokenhearted (kaah)'; type (102) 'status', role (115) characteristic. The bearer (105) is 'the brokenhearted'. The operation (106) is 'be pursued to death' - the crushed in spirit hounded to the grave. The target (107) is present: 'by the enemy'. In this row coupling (112) and locus (116) values appear transposed with their labels (coupling holds 'internal:ib-state', locus holds 'paired with the poor and needy'); read faithfully, the broken-heartedness is a state WITHIN the inner being, PAIRED with 'the poor and needy' (the v16 triad). The movement: the crushed-in-spirit (bearer) -> pursued to death (operation) -> by the enemy (target) -> joined to the poor and needy (coupling). The discovery (114): the crushed in spirit the enemy hounded to the grave. Silences: seat (104) 'none'; manner (108) 'none'; source (103), intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) absent - no rescue-effect here; the enemy's cruelty is the point. Compared with H7665:brokenheart (Ps 34:18, 147:3, where the broken heart draws God's nearness and healing), this kaah-reading shows the SAME interior condition being exploited by a human enemy rather than met by God - a sharp distinction (directive 8): brokenness that in one context invites divine tenderness here invites the oppressor's final blow. On the inner-being lens, the arena is the persecutor, and the finding (directive 6) is grim - the enemy pressed hardest exactly where the victim was already most broken.
narratives.story: The poet charges his enemy with a chilling cruelty: he chased a person whose heart was already crushed, hounding the brokenhearted all the way to death. Here a shattered heart, instead of drawing compassion, drew the killer's pursuit. This broken condition stands alongside poverty and need - the victim was low in every way. It is a stark contrast to other poems where a broken heart brings God close; here the same wound only invited the final blow. The enemy struck hardest exactly where the victim was weakest.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'poor (ani)'; type (102) 'status', role (115) characteristic. The bearer (105) is 'the poor'. The operation (106) is 'be pursued' - the afflicted hunted. The target (107) is present: 'by the enemy'. In this row coupling (112) and locus (116) values appear transposed with their labels (coupling holds 'internal:ib-state', locus holds 'paired with the needy and brokenhearted'); read faithfully, the poverty is a state WITHIN the inner being, PAIRED with 'the needy and brokenhearted' - completing the v16 triad. The movement: the afflicted (bearer) -> pursued (operation) -> by the wicked enemy (target) -> joined to the needy and brokenhearted (coupling). The discovery (114): the afflicted victim the enemy hounded. Silences: seat (104) 'none'; manner (108) 'none'; source (103), intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) absent - no rescue-effect; the enemy's crime is the focus. On the inner-being lens, the arena is the persecutor whose interior is exposed (directive 5, 6): he did not remember to show kindness but pursued the poor. This reading, with its passage-mates (needy #6, brokenhearted H3512), shows the family's poverty-cluster in its most vulnerable role - the low as prey, their weakness the very thing the malicious exploited.
narratives.story: The poet condemns his enemy for chasing down a poor, afflicted man instead of showing kindness. Here poverty marks a helpless victim - one of three words (poor, needy, brokenhearted) painting a person low in every way. The very weakness that should have stirred mercy is what the enemy preyed upon. This exposes the cruelty of the oppressor's heart: he hunted the defenceless rather than sparing them. It is lowliness at its most exposed - poverty turned into a target.
narratives.variation_note: One of six readings of H6041:poor (ani). Here (Ps 109:16) the poor are the AFFLICTED VICTIM the enemy hounded ('pursued the poor'), operation 'be pursued', target 'by the enemy'. It differs from #1 (confident lowliness), #2 (grounding plea), #3 (turning to praise), #4 (claim on God), #6 (pleading against foes). Distinctive: poverty as the mark of a persecuted victim, part of the v16 triad (poor, needy, brokenhearted) the wicked exploited.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'needy (ebyon)'; type (102) 'status', role (115) characteristic. The bearer (105) is 'the psalmist'. The operation (106) is 'be needy' - the owned condition. The target (107) is present: 'before God' - the neediness is presented Godward as the ground of appeal. In this row coupling (112) and locus (116) values appear transposed with their labels (coupling holds 'internal:ib-state', locus holds 'paired with being poor'); read faithfully, neediness is a state WITHIN the inner being, PAIRED with 'being poor'. The movement: the destitute self (bearer) -> owns its neediness (operation) -> lays it before God (target) -> twinned with poverty (coupling). The discovery (114): the destitution the psalmist pleads. Silences: seat (104) 'none'; manner (108) 'none'; source (103), intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) absent - no separate effect beyond the plea. On the inner-being lens, God is the arena. The striking distinction (directive 8, 10) from #6 in the same passage: at v16 the poor-and-needy were the enemy's victims; at v22 the psalmist claims that very estate as his own, turning the description of the hounded low into a first-person confession that grounds his cry to God. The same lowliness that the wicked exploited becomes the psalmist's leverage before God.
narratives.story: Having exposed how his enemy hunted the poor, the poet now turns and says of himself: 'I am poor and needy.' He claims the very low estate he described in the victims, making it his own plea before God. His neediness, paired with his poverty, is laid openly before God as the reason he should be helped. What the enemy treated as an opportunity to attack, the poet treats as his ground for asking grace. The same weakness that drew persecution now becomes his appeal to God.
narratives.variation_note: Seventh of eight readings of H0034:needy (ebyon). Here (Ps 109:22) neediness is the psalmist's OWN plea before God ('For I am poor and needy'), operation 'be needy', target 'before God'. It differs from #1 (heard), #2 (urgent plea), #3 (deliver from wicked), #4 (casting self on God), #5 (raised), #6 (pursued as victim), #8 (lifted). Distinctive: after describing the enemy's persecution of the poor (v16), the psalmist now claims that same low estate for himself before God - the victim's confession turned into a prayer-claim.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'poor (ani)'; type (102) 'status', role (115) characteristic. The bearer (105) is 'the psalmist'. The operation (106) is 'be poor' - the owned condition. The target (107) is present: 'before God'. In this row coupling (112) and locus (116) values appear transposed with their labels (coupling holds 'internal:ib-state', locus holds 'paired with being needy and the stricken heart'); read faithfully, the poverty is a state WITHIN the inner being, PAIRED with 'being needy and the stricken heart' - the fullest coupling of any poor-reading, joining poverty, need, and a wounded interior. The movement: the afflicted self (bearer) -> owns its poverty (operation) -> before God (target) -> bound to neediness and a stricken heart (coupling). The discovery (114): the psalmist's lowliness, his plea's ground, set against his powerful foes. Silences: seat (104) 'none' (though the coupling names the stricken heart, the seat row itself is unfilled); manner (108) 'none'; source (103), intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) absent - no separate effect beyond the plea. On the inner-being lens, God is the arena the poor self appeals to, against the backdrop of mighty enemies. The variation from #5 (same passage) is the whole finding (directive 10): at v16 the poor is the enemy's victim; at v22 the poor is the psalmist's own confessed identity, now joined to a heart 'stricken within' - poverty deepened into interior wounding, offered to God as the ground of rescue.
narratives.story: The poet confesses openly: 'I am poor and needy, and my heart is wounded within me.' Here his poverty is joined to his need and to a heart that has been struck - the fullest picture of his brokenness, laid before God while powerful enemies press around him. Earlier he described the poor being hunted; now he owns that same poverty as his own, but adds the ache inside. His lowliness is not just outward want; it reaches into a wounded heart. All of it he offers to God as the reason to be saved.
narratives.variation_note: One of six readings of H6041:poor (ani). Here (Ps 109:22) poverty is the psalmist's OWN confession set against his powerful foes ('For I am poor and needy'), operation 'be poor', target 'before God', paired with being needy and 'the stricken heart' (v22b: 'my heart is stricken within me'). It differs from #1 (confident), #2 (grounding plea), #3 (praise), #4 (claim on God), #5 (pursued victim). Distinctive: this reading uniquely ties the poverty to the psalmist's wounded heart, and sets it against his mighty enemies - lowliness owned in the very passage where the poor were shown persecuted (#5, v16).

narratives.narrative: This reading (a distinct char_key, H0034:needyon 'needy one') is the RESOLVED counterpart to the persecution earlier in Ps 109 - the needy one DEFENDED by God. The sense (101) is 'needy one (ebyon)'; type (102) 'status', role (115) characteristic. The bearer (105) is 'the needy one'. The operation (106) is 'be defended' - God's protective act. The target (107) is present: 'by God at his right hand'. In this row coupling (112) and locus (116) values appear transposed with their labels (coupling holds 'internal:ib-state', locus holds 'paired with the soul saved'); read faithfully, the neediness is a state WITHIN the inner being, PAIRED with 'the soul saved' - God's standing-by issues in the soul's rescue. The movement: the needy one (bearer) -> defended (operation) -> by God who stands at his right hand (target) -> bound to the soul's salvation (coupling). The discovery (114): the poor whom God defends, standing where the accuser stood (v6) - a deliberate inversion: in v6 an accuser stands at the wicked's right hand; here God stands at the needy one's right hand. Silences: seat (104) 'none'; manner (108) 'none'; source (103), intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) absent - no separate effect beyond the defence/salvation. On the inner-being lens, God is the arena and champion: the needy one's low estate, exploited by the enemy earlier in the psalm, is now the very position God takes His stand beside. This closes the psalm's arc (directive 10 across the passage): the hounded poor of v16 becomes the defended needy one of v31 - lowliness vindicated, God taking the advocate's place the accuser once held.
narratives.story: The psalm ends on a note of rescue: God stands at the right hand of the needy one to defend and save him. Earlier an accuser had stood at that same right-hand place to condemn - now God takes it to protect. Here neediness is a low estate that God himself comes to champion, and his standing-by means the person's very life is saved. The one who was hunted for his poverty is now guarded by God. It is the turning of the whole poem: the defenceless finds a defender in God.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'needy (ebyon)'; type (102) 'status', role (115) characteristic. The bearer (105) is 'the needy'. The operation (106) is 'be lifted' - God's raising act. The target (107) is present: 'from the ash heap by God'. In this row coupling (112) and locus (116) values appear transposed with their labels (coupling holds 'internal:ib-state', locus holds 'paired with the poor raised from the dust'); read faithfully, the neediness is a state WITHIN the inner being, PAIRED with 'the poor raised from the dust' (v7's parallel line, H1800). The movement: the destitute (bearer) -> lifted (operation) -> from the ash heap by God (target) -> twinned with the poor raised from the dust (coupling), to sit with princes (v8). The discovery (114): the destitute God raises to sit with princes. Silences: seat (104) 'none'; manner (108) 'none'; source (103), intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) absent - no separate effect beyond the lifting/enthronement. On the inner-being lens, God is the arena and agent who stoops (v6, 'he looks far down') to raise the lowest. This reading closes the family's brightest arc: from ash heap to princes, the needy exalted - the mirror image of Ps 88's unrelieved helplessness (directive 5, both weighed). Paired with H1800 'poor' in the same verse, it doubles the picture of God's reversal.
narratives.story: This joyful psalm pictures God stooping down from heaven to lift the needy right out of the ash heap - the rubbish pile - and set them among princes. Here neediness is the lowest imaginable place, and it is exactly where God reaches to raise people up. The needy stand together with the poor lifted from the dust, a doubled image of God's great reversal. Nothing is said about how they sank so low; the wonder is entirely in the lifting. From the ash heap to a place of honour - this is God delighting to exalt the lowest.
narratives.variation_note: Eighth of eight readings of H0034:needy (ebyon). Here (Ps 113:7) the needy are LIFTED FROM THE ASH HEAP ('lifts the needy from the ash heap'), operation 'be lifted', target 'from the ash heap by God'. It differs from #1 (heard), #2 (urgent plea), #3 (deliver from wicked), #4 (casting self on God), #5 (raised out of affliction), #6 (pursued victim), #7 (pleading before God). Distinctive: the extreme reversal - from the ash heap to sitting with princes - God's characteristic exaltation of the lowest.

narratives.narrative: This is a distinct Hebrew word for 'poor' (dal, low/weak - not ani or ebyon). The sense (101) is 'poor (dal)'; type (102) 'status', role (115) characteristic. The bearer (105) is 'the poor'. The operation (106) is 'be raised' - God's lifting act. The target (107) is present: 'from the dust by God'. In this row coupling (112) and locus (116) values appear transposed with their labels (coupling holds 'internal:ib-state', locus holds 'paired with the needy lifted from the ash heap'); read faithfully, the poverty is a state WITHIN the inner being, PAIRED with 'the needy lifted from the ash heap' (v7's parallel line, H0034 #8). The movement: the lowly (bearer) -> raised (operation) -> from the dust by God (target) -> twinned with the needy from the ash heap (coupling). The discovery (114): the lowly whom God lifts, the first object of his great reversal. Silences: seat (104) 'none'; manner (108) 'none'; source (103), intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) absent - no separate effect beyond the raising. On the inner-being lens, God is the arena and agent stooping to lift. The distinction from its verse-twin 'needy' (H0034, ebyon) is a finding (directive 8): dal ('low from the dust') and ebyon ('needy from the ash heap') form a synonymous pair, two words for the same lifted lowliness, doubling the image of reversal - God raises the low from the dust and the needy from the refuse to enthrone them with princes.
narratives.story: The psalm celebrates God raising the poor from the dust - the lowest, weakest people - and setting them high. Here poverty is a condition of being brought down to the ground, and God's delight is to lift it up. This line runs in parallel with the needy being lifted from the ash heap: two ways of saying the same wonderful thing. God stoops to the very bottom and raises the humble to sit among princes. It is a portrait of the God who overturns low places and honours the least.

narratives.narrative: This char_key (H0034:poor) reads ebyon as 'poor' (the same word elsewhere glossed 'needy'), here the poor of ZION SATISFIED WITH BREAD ('I will satisfy her poor with bread'). The sense (101) is 'poor (ebyon)'; type (102) 'status', role (115) characteristic. The bearer (105) is 'the poor of Zion'. The operation (106) is 'be satisfied' - God's provisioning act. The target (107) is present: 'with bread by God'. In this row coupling (112) and locus (116) values appear transposed with their labels (coupling holds 'internal:ib-state', locus holds 'paired with God satisfying them'); read faithfully, the poverty is a state WITHIN the inner being, PAIRED with 'God satisfying them'. The movement: the poor of Zion (bearer) -> satisfied (operation) -> with bread by God (target) -> bound to God's provision (coupling), at the place of his chosen rest. The discovery (114): the needy of Zion whom God fills; the low lifted at the place of his rest. Silences: seat (104) 'none'; manner (108) 'none'; source (103), intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) absent - no separate effect beyond the satisfying. On the inner-being lens, God is the arena and provider: here lowliness is met not by rescue from enemies or exaltation over them, but by simple abundant provision - God's promise to feed Zion's poor at the dwelling he has chosen. It rounds out the family's poverty-cluster with the note of settled sufficiency: the low are filled.
narratives.story: In this psalm about God choosing Zion as his home, he promises to satisfy her poor with bread. Here the poor are the needy people of God's own city, and his answer to their poverty is plain, abundant provision - they will be fed. Their lack is met not by rescue from enemies but by God simply filling them at the place he has made his dwelling. It is a quiet, homely picture of grace: the hungry poor given enough. Where God settles, the lowly are satisfied.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'lowly (shaphal)'; type (102) 'status', role (115) characteristic. The bearer (105) is 'the lowly'. The operation (106) is 'be regarded' - God's attentive act. The target (107) is present: 'by God'. In this row coupling (112) and locus (116) values appear transposed with their labels (coupling holds 'internal:ib-state', locus holds 'paired with the haughty God knows from afar'); read faithfully, lowliness is a state WITHIN the inner being, PAIRED with 'the haughty God knows from afar' - the antithesis that defines it (v6b: 'but the haughty he knows from afar'). The movement: the lowly (bearer) -> regarded/drawn near (operation) -> by the high God (target) -> set against the haughty kept at a distance (coupling). The discovery (114): the operation of divine attention inverting rank - the high God draws near to the low, not the great. Silences: seat (104) 'none'; manner (108) 'none'; source (103), intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) absent - no cause traced, no grading, no qualifier, no separate effect beyond the regarding. On the inner-being lens, God is the arena: the finding (directive 5, both poles weighed) is a deliberate inversion of expected rank - though the LORD is high, it is the low he regards and the proud he keeps at arm's length. This crystallises the whole family's logic: lowliness draws divine nearness, height/pride pushes it away.
narratives.story: The poet captures the paradox at the heart of it all: though God is exalted high above everything, it is the lowly he pays attention to. The humble, low-placed person is exactly the one the high God draws near to regard. And the opposite is just as true: the proud, for all their height, he keeps at a distance, knowing them only from afar. So rank is turned upside down - nearness to God goes not to the great but to the small. This one line sums up the whole pattern: lowliness pulls God close; pride pushes him away.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'the brokenhearted healed'; type (102) 'state', role (115) characteristic, locus (116) internal:ib-state - the shattered heart read as a real inner condition. The bearer (105) is 'the wounded'. The operation (106) is God's: 'the broken heart and its wounds are the object of God's healing - inner injury bound up'; the target (107) is 'heart-woundedness'; the coupling (112) is brokenhearted-healed. The movement: the wounded interior (condition) -> God heals and binds up (operation) -> heart-woundedness as target -> bound to healing (coupling). The discovery (114): the interior wound (a shattered heart) is named as what God mends; the inner injury is real and addressed. Silences: seat (104) 'none' - though 'heart' is in the verse, the coding treats the woundedness as the whole inner person's, not an isolated organ; manner (108) 'none'. Source (103), intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) absent: no cause of the wounding traced, no grading, no qualifier, no separate effect beyond the healing, no prohibition. On the inner-being lens, God is the arena and physician: the broken heart is not merely comforted by nearness (as in Ps 34:18) but actively repaired - the wound bound up. The variation from #1 is a finding (directive 10): the same interior brokenness invites, in one place, God's drawing-near, and in another, God's healing - two facets of how the shattered inner being is met.
narratives.story: This psalm of praise says God heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds - like a doctor tending an injury. Here a shattered heart is treated as a real inner wound, and God's response is to mend it, not just to sit nearby. The injury is genuine and named, and God actively repairs it. Where another poem pictured God simply drawing close to the crushed, this one shows him binding the wound and making it whole. Both are true: the broken heart both draws God near and gets healed by him.
narratives.variation_note: One of two readings of H7665:brokenheart. Here (Ps 147:3) the broken heart is the object of God's HEALING ('he heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds'); operation is the wound bound up, target 'heart-woundedness', locus internal:ib-state. It differs from #1 (Ps 34:18), where the broken heart draws God's NEARNESS and saving. Same shattered interior, two divine responses: there proximity/rescue, here medical mending - so brokenness is both the place God comes close and the wound he actively repairs.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'the humble lifted up'; type (102) 'state', role (115) characteristic, locus (116) internal:ib-state. The bearer (105) is 'the humble'. The operation (106) is God's: 'the humble are the ones God lifts up while casting the wicked to the ground'; the target (107) is 'humility'; the coupling (112) is humble-lifted. The movement: the lowly interior (condition) -> God lifts up (operation) -> humility as the posture raised (target) -> bound to lifting (coupling), set against the wicked cast down. The discovery (114): the interior lowliness is what God raises; humility is the posture met with lifting. Silences: seat (104) 'none'; manner (108) 'none'; source (103), intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) absent: no origin of the humility traced, no grading, no qualifier, no separate effect beyond the lifting, no prohibition. On the inner-being lens, God is the arena and agent: the same divine act sorts two interiors (directive 5, no valence bias) - it raises the humble and floors the wicked. This joins Ps 138:6's inversion of rank and Ps 76:9's saving judgment: God's characteristic movement lifts the low precisely as it brings down the proud. Lowliness is not weakness to be pitied here but the posture God actively exalts.
narratives.story: This psalm declares that God lifts up the humble and throws the wicked down to the ground. In one and the same act he sorts two kinds of people: the lowly he raises, the arrogant he floors. Here humility is a settled inner posture, and it is exactly what God chooses to exalt. Nothing is said about how a person became humble; the focus is on God's response - lifting. The picture is clear and even-handed: to be low before God is to be raised; to be proud is to be brought down.
narratives.variation_note: One of five readings of H6035:humbl (anav). Here (Ps 147:6) the humble are LIFTED UP while the wicked are cast down ('the LORD lifts up the humble; he casts the wicked to the ground'); operation is the lifting, target 'humility', locus internal:ib-state. It differs from #1 (led/taught), #2 (see and be glad), #3 (saved in judgment), #5 (adorned). Distinctive: the explicit two-way movement - the humble raised, the wicked floored - lowliness met with lifting in the same act that abases pride (directive 5).

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'the humble adorned'; type (102) 'state', role (115) characteristic, locus (116) internal:ib-state. The bearer (105) is 'the humble'. The operation (106) is God's: 'the humble are the ones God beautifies with salvation - lowliness crowned'; the target (107) is 'humility'; the coupling (112) is humble-adorned. The movement: the lowly interior (condition) -> God delights in and adorns it (operation) -> humility as the beautified state (target) -> bound to adornment (coupling). The discovery (114): the interior lowliness is what God delights in and dresses with rescue. Silences: seat (104) 'none'; manner (108) 'none'; source (103), intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) absent: no origin traced, no grading, no qualifier, no separate effect beyond the adorning/salvation, no prohibition. On the inner-being lens, God is the arena: this reading adds delight and beauty to the family's pattern - not only does God lead (Ps 25:9), save (Ps 76:9), lift (Ps 147:6) the humble, here he takes pleasure in them and crowns them with salvation. It is the warmest terminus of the five anav-readings: lowliness met not merely with help but with God's own delight, dressed in rescue like an adornment.
narratives.story: This final praise-psalm reaches the warmest note: God takes delight in the humble and adorns them with salvation, like dressing them in beauty. Here lowliness is not just rescued or lifted but treasured - God actually enjoys the humble and crowns them with his help. Their low posture becomes the very thing God delights to beautify. Nothing is said about how they became humble; the wonder is God's pleasure in them. Of all the pictures of the lowly, this is the tenderest: the humble, delighted in and dressed in rescue.
narratives.variation_note: One of five readings of H6035:humbl (anav). Here (Ps 149:4) the humble are ADORNED/CROWNED with salvation ('he adorns the humble with salvation'); operation is the beautifying, target 'humility', locus internal:ib-state. It differs from #1 (led/taught), #2 (see and be glad), #3 (saved in judgment), #4 (lifted up). Distinctive: the tenderest note of the five - God takes pleasure in the humble and dresses them with rescue, beauty added to the lowly, not merely rescue or exaltation.
